messages:
olivia: Heads-up — onboarding sample hits a reproducible failure. Start a long-running Generator.Stream, then trigger token rotation (we simulate refresh). The iterator stops with an opaque EOF-like error.
kevin: Interesting. Do you recreate the http.Client when you rotate the token? That will tear the underlying connection and the server will close streams.
olivia: Yeah, we swapped the client because our KMS hook returns a full creds struct. We did that to keep sample code simple.
sam: That is the classic footgun. Better pattern: keep one http.Transport and inject a token per-request with a RoundTripper. Avoids TLS reconnection on refresh.
olivia: Can you paste the minimal RoundTripper pattern? I'll update the sample.
sam: Sure — tiny snippet: 
```go
// tokenProvider reads token from cache (updated by background refresh)
rt := &authRoundTripper{base: http.DefaultTransport, tokenProvider: tokenProvider}
client := &http.Client{Transport: rt}
// client reused across refreshes
```
This way tokenProvider() can return the latest token without recreating connections.
kevin: SDK-side thought: the Go generator iterator currently returns a generic error like "rpc error: code = Canceled desc = stream terminated by peer" when connection dies. New users interpret that as normal completion. We should surface a richer error classification (ErrStreamAuthRotate, ErrStreamConnReset) so apps can distinguish cases.
olivia: Exactly — QA hit this and filed a ticket because they thought the stream finished. The raw string is: "rpc error: code = Canceled desc = stream terminated by peer".
sam: Two immediate actions: 1) Update onboarding sample to show the RoundTripper approach, and 2) add a helper in the Go SDK (StreamWithAuthRefresh) that optionally retries once on auth-rotation or returns a typed error so callers can handle retry explicitly.
kevin: For the helper API, sketch: StreamWithAuthRefresh(ctx, req, opts) where opts.RetryOnAuthRotate bool. Behavior: if handshake fails due to token rejection mid-stream, either transparently retry the request once or return ErrStreamAuthRotate. Also provide context cancellation safeguards.
olivia: If we add that helper and the sample, it will cut down support questions. New users copy the sample and hit this race.
sam: Also add a short note in generator README: "If you must recreate client on token refresh, cancel ongoing iterators and restart them — or prefer RoundTripper token injection." Add example backoff/notify pattern.
devex-bot: created ticket DEVEX-907: go-sdk: add typed stream errors + onboarding sample update (link) :white_check_mark:
kevin: I'll add a small regression test that simulates server rejecting the midstream token and verifies helper behavior. Olivia — can you attach the repro logs to DEVEX-907?
olivia: Yep, uploading logs now and will open a docs PR to show both patterns (reuse transport vs explicit restart with user-visible message). Thanks all :thumbsup:
